blocks.name: immediate_generator
blocks.responsibility: Generate sign-extended I-, S-, B-, and J-type immediates, and the zero-extended U-type immediate from the instruction word.
blocks.design_rationale: Centralizes immediate bit mapping and sign extension, making branch, jump, load/store, and ALU-immediate behavior independently verifiable.

blocks.name: register_file
blocks.responsibility: Provide 32 32-bit integer registers with two asynchronous read ports, one rising-edge write port, asynchronous active-high reset, and hardwired-zero x0.
blocks.design_rationale: Isolates architectural state and asynchronous operand reads, keeping the single-cycle datapath simple and register behavior easy to test.

blocks.name: alu
blocks.responsibility: Perform RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and signed and unsigned comparisons selected by an operation control input.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeps datapath operations and comparison semantics in one combinational block, supporting focused verification and avoiding unnecessary pipeline state.

blocks.name: decoder
blocks.responsibility: Decode RV32I instruction opcode and function fields into register-write, memory-write, operand-source, ALU-operation, branch, jump, and writeback-selection controls.
blocks.design_rationale: Separates instruction decoding from datapath execution, improving control-path readability and making instruction coverage easier to verify.

blocks.name: cpu
blocks.responsibility: Implement the RV32I single-cycle top level: maintain the PC, instantiate the register file, decoder, ALU, and immediate generator, select branch and jump targets, perform load extraction and extension, and drive the instruction and data buses exactly as specified.
blocks.design_rationale: Provides the required bus-only interface and integrates the combinational datapath with edge-triggered architectural state for one-instruction-per-cycle execution.

notes: Use only ieee.std_logic_1164 and ieee.numeric_std. The decoder's wb_select encodings should distinguish ALU result, load data, PC+4, and U-immediate; AUIPC uses PC as the ALU first operand. Branch conditions use funct3 together with the ALU comparison outputs. Stores drive the unshifted rs2 value and select byte, halfword, or word width; loads select and extend the addressed subword from the asynchronously supplied aligned word.
